newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia seeks meat export guidelines with China.
newsitem.headline: Australia seeks meat export guidelines with China.

text.p: The Australian government wanted to agree on official guidelines with China for the export of beef and cattle, a spokesman for the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said on Friday.
Australia's beef exports to China were comparatively small at present and Australia wanted to export more, the spokesman told Reuters.
The guidelines, or protocols, would cover some quarantine restrictions and other non-tariff barriers, he said.

Australia was "pushing ahead" with the negotiations and regarded protocols recently signed by Canada with China for beef exports as "a positive sign in general" for the opening of the Chinese market, he said.

Australia exported 1,628 tonnes of beef to China last year and already sold directly to specialised joint venture processing operations as well as into the top-end of the hotel and food servicing sector.

"China offers a lot of long-term potential and all major countries are investigating how to position themselves to take advantage of that long-term potential," Steve Martyn, deputy general manager beef marketing of the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp (AMLC), told Reuters.
Australia already did many promotions with hotels in China and also with top-end supermarkets, he also said.

Asked whether the recent Canadian protocol would threaten Australia's position in the Chinese industry, Martyn said that Australia's present sales significantly outweighed Canada's sales of 923 tonnes in calendar 1996.
Martyn also said Australian protocol negotiations with China focused on quarantine issues mainly covering live cattle exports.
China was a net exporter of cattle, saw a future in that trade and was seeking to build its 110 million-head herd into a more exportable product, he said.
Canada was still a comparatively minor exporter of beef to Asia, but its exports to the region were growing and the country was showing an increasing interest in the market, he said.
Australia exported a total 738,000 tonnes of beef and veal in 1995/96, with largest market Japan taking 319,000 tonnes, the U.S. 183,000 tonnes and the third-largest market South Korea 57,000 tonnes.
Canada's Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said earlier this week that Canada had become the first nation to sign a beef import protocol with China.
The protocol sets terms and conditions under which Canadian producers may export beef products directly to China's retail market.
The review and approval of exporting establishments by Chinese authorities had yet to be finalized but criteria for exporting plants should be set this year, Goodale said.

"Any inroads into the vast Chinese beef market can only be good news for Canadian producers. Getting into China before our major trading partners provides a real opportunity for increased sales of Canadian beef," Canadian Cattlemen's Association president Dave Andrews said.

Canada sold 923 tonnes of beef to China in calendar 1996, down 8.5 percent from 1,009 tonnes in 1995 but aims to sell 6,000 tonnes by the year 2000, or the equivalent of 36,000 head of cattle, the Canada Beef Export Federation said.
